lines: (Biscuit leans on Yusuf's shin until the phone call is over.)
(Yusuf says his name to Mum. Biscuit sits up very straight.)
(A long phone call. Biscuit uses it to sniff one geranium.)
(Biscuit hears goodnight on the phone. Gives a tiny woof back.)
(Yusuf laughs at the phone. Biscuit laughs too, with his tail.)
(Biscuit lies down mid-call. This is a two-geranium call.)
(Biscuit holds the lead in his mouth. He will wait. Nicely.)
(The phone glows blue. Biscuit glows a little too, inside.)
(Biscuit sniffs Yusuf's pocket. The phone is in there. Hm.)
(Biscuit watches the moths while Yusuf chats to Mum.)
(Phone call. Biscuit counts the lemons on the tree. Three.)
(Yusuf tells Mum about tomorrow. Biscuit hears park. Ears up.)
(Biscuit pretends the jasmine is talking to him too.)
(Mum is describing her garden. Biscuit would like to visit.)
(Biscuit rests his chin on the step. Long call. Nice call.)
(Yusuf turns in a slow circle on the phone. Biscuit follows.)
(Biscuit gives the phone one polite sniff. It smells of Mum.)
(Biscuit remembers Mum's kitchen. The good floor. The crumbs.)
(Biscuit sits under a lemon tree, guarding Yusuf's phone call.)
(The call ends. Biscuit stands at once. Off we go, then.)
(Biscuit sneezes at a petal during the call. Sorry, Mum.)
(Biscuit sniffs the bougainvillea. Pink. Very pink. Yes.)
(Biscuit stops at the lemon tree. Checks it is still there.)
(Biscuit finds a fallen petal and carries it like a medal.)
(Biscuit sniffs the night jasmine. Closes his eyes. Ah.)
(A geranium pot. Biscuit sniffs it twice. All good.)
(Biscuit greets a rosemary bush by name. It is Rosemary.)
(Biscuit lies in the lavender bed's shadow. Smells lovely.)
(Biscuit noses a fallen lemon along the path. A small parade.)
(The basil on the café sill. Biscuit nods to it every evening.)
(Biscuit sniffs a terracotta pot. Warm still. From the sun.)
(One bougainvillea petal on his nose. Biscuit keeps very still.)
(Biscuit has found the mint. He tells everyone with his tail.)
(Biscuit sits by the planter. Someone watered it. Good work.)
(Biscuit walks the long way past the roses. His idea.)
(Biscuit sniffs the olive tree. Old friend. Very old friend.)
(Biscuit admires the oleander. From a respectful distance.)
(The cypress smells of evening. Biscuit agrees with it.)
(Biscuit plans tomorrow: lemon tree, bakery, lemon tree.)
(Tomorrow, Biscuit will find the stick again. He knows where.)
(Biscuit is saving one sniff of the fountain for tomorrow.)
(Biscuit hid a crust under the palm. For later. Probably.)
(Biscuit sits facing home. Not yet. But he is ready.)
(Biscuit hears the lantern clink by the door. Soon. Soon!)
(Biscuit dreams about tomorrow's baguette. Awake, even.)
(Biscuit remembers being small. The step was so tall then.)
(Biscuit remembers his first lemon. Sour. Still friends.)
(The bench where Biscuit learned to sit. He sits there now.)
(Biscuit remembers the day he met Yusuf. Best sniff ever.)
(A small, contented huff. The kind dogs save for evenings.)
(The string lights come on. Biscuit wags at each bulb.)
(Biscuit watches the lamps light, one by one. Counting.)
(The sky goes blue. Biscuit's nose goes up. Lovely air.)
(Biscuit sits under the string lights, looking festive.)
(Blue hour. Biscuit's favourite colour, he has decided.)
(Biscuit trots in a figure of eight. For joy.)
(A moth visits Biscuit's nose. They part as friends.)
(Biscuit hears the café spoons. Notes it. Does not beg.)
(Biscuit lifts one paw. A polite question for the waiter.)
(Biscuit stretches long, front paws first. Then the back.)
(Biscuit sits on the warm stone. The stone is happy too.)
(Tail goes thump, thump, thump on the promenade.)
(Biscuit rolls on the cool grass. Rolls back. Perfect.)
(Odile says bonsoir. Biscuit bows. A very small bow.)
(Biscuit hears Lucie's bell somewhere. Two dings. For him.)
(Biscuit sniffs Camille's handbag. Roses inside. Lovely.)
(Inès jogs past. Biscuit jogs three steps with her. Enough.)
(Biscuit sits beside the neighbour's bench. Company.)
(A visitor crouches down. Biscuit gives the full wag.)
(Biscuit leads Yusuf to the flower boxes. Important tour.)
(Biscuit sniffs the window box. The petunias say hello.)
(Biscuit pauses at every planter. Roll call of flowers.)
(Biscuit lies beneath the lemon tree as if he planted it.)
(A lemon leaf falls. Biscuit catches it. Gently. Good dog.)
(Biscuit sniffs the pot of thyme. Then again. To be sure.)
(The hibiscus is closing for the night. Biscuit whispers woof.)
(Biscuit sits up straight under the lamp. Evening portrait.)
(Biscuit looks at the first star. Then at Yusuf. Shows him.)
(Biscuit chooses a different lamp post tonight. Adventurous.)
(Biscuit has a pebble. It is his pebble now. Forever.)
(Biscuit sniffs the fountain rim. Tomorrow's coin wishes.)
(Biscuit follows a petal down the promenade. It wins.)
(Biscuit leans into a scratch behind the ear. Bliss.)
(Biscuit sniffs a sun-warm lemon. Leaves it for a person.)
(Biscuit has a little yawn. Not tired. Just evening.)
(Biscuit waits while Yusuf talks to Mum. Patience: medium.)
(Yusuf says 'yes, Mum'. Biscuit's tail says it too.)
(Biscuit tilts his head. Is Mum in the little box?)
(Biscuit barks once, softly, so Mum knows he is here.)
(Biscuit hears his name in the call. Ears up. Famous.)
(Biscuit studies a lamppost while the humans talk.)
(Yusuf points at the sky for Mum. Biscuit points his nose too.)
(Biscuit circles three times and settles beside the call.)
(A cobblestone, sniffed thoroughly while Yusuf says goodbye.)
(Biscuit hears 'one more thing'. Lies down again.)
(Biscuit waits by the column. The column waits too.)
(Biscuit hears 'bye, bye, bye'. Stands. Too early. Sits.)
(Biscuit's lead goes slack. A call is a little rest stop.)
(A gull on the railing. Biscuit and the gull share the view.)
(The cat on the wall blinks slowly. Biscuit blinks quickly.)
(Biscuit drinks from the fountain, delicately, like a gentleman.)
(The town clock chimes. Biscuit counts along. Loses count at two.)
(Biscuit sits under the café awning, in case of crumbs.)
(Biscuit admires a shutter. Blue, like the sky now.)
(Biscuit trots over the blue tiles. Click click click.)
(A lamp comes on above Biscuit. He looks up, impressed.)
(Biscuit sniffs a palm tree. Nods. Same palm as yesterday.)
(Biscuit finds the warm patch where the sun used to be.)
(Biscuit's shadow is long and blue. He likes it very much.)
(Biscuit sniffs Henri's shoe. Café, lemon, crossword.)
(Biscuit sits beside Odile's bench, very straight. A guard.)
(Biscuit hears a cork pop at the café. Ears up. Not for him.)
(The gulls go to bed. Biscuit sees them off with a nod.)
(Biscuit sniffs a cypress. Tall tree, important smells.)
(The cat on the wall yawns. Biscuit yawns. Contagious.)
(Biscuit checks under the bench. A crumb. A blue-hour crumb.)
(Biscuit trots to the railing and back. Just to check the sea.)
(A geranium leans out of a window box. Biscuit sniffs hello.)
(Biscuit sneezes at a lavender pot. Bless him.)
(Biscuit hears Marcel stacking chairs somewhere. Tail: on.)
(Biscuit sits by the kiosk shutter. Closed. He waits anyway.)
(Biscuit discovers his own reflection in the café window. Hello!)
(Biscuit sniffs the evening air. Sea salt, rosé, bread.)
(Biscuit chooses a cobblestone. Lies on it. His now.)
(Biscuit's tag jingles on the tiles. A tiny bell for evening.)
(Biscuit watches the fountain catch the lamplight. Sparkly water.)
(A gull lands. Biscuit stands very still. The gull also.)
(Biscuit hears Lucie's laugh. Turns. Wags in her direction.)
(Biscuit sniffs the zinc drainpipe. Rooftop news, fresh.)
(Biscuit sits under the clock. It is exactly Biscuit o'clock.)
(Biscuit greets every chair leg at the café. Thorough.)
(Biscuit lies across the doorway. A very small draught stopper.)
(Biscuit watches the sky go from blue to bluer. Approves both.)
(Biscuit listens to the fountain. Splash, splash, nap, almost.)
(Biscuit finds a pinecone under a cypress. Treasure.)
(Biscuit trots past the bakery. Closed, but still smells kind.)
(Biscuit stares at the moon. The moon is a very round biscuit.)
(Biscuit wags at a passing jogger. Inès waves. A good trade.)
(Biscuit sits on the promenade like a small statue.)
(A shutter creaks closed above. Biscuit says goodnight to it.)
(Biscuit follows a moth for three steps. Then lets it go.)
(Biscuit sniffs Théo's trouser hem. Rosé, sand, children.)
(Biscuit sits for Camille. Gets a scratch. Sits again, hopeful.)
(Biscuit hears a glass clink. Clinks his tag in reply.)
(Biscuit's ears go pink in the last of the light. Then blue.)
(Biscuit finds a gull feather. Keeps it. A souvenir.)
(Biscuit sniffs an awning pole. Striped smell. Probably.)
(The cat jumps down. The cat walks past. Biscuit is honoured.)
(Biscuit finds a dropped olive. Inspects. Leaves it for a gull.)
(Biscuit wags at a window as its light comes on. Hello, house.)
(Biscuit sits by the fountain fish. They stare. A good evening.)
(Biscuit hears music from the café. One ear dances.)
(Biscuit trots in a straight line, then a zigzag. Free verse.)
(Biscuit sniffs a bench slat. Henri sat here. Recently.)
(Biscuit does a small happy hop over a puddle from the fountain.)
(Biscuit lies down facing the sea. Back to the town. Trusts it.)
(Biscuit chases his tail once. Catches the evening instead.)
(Biscuit sits with his nose in the breeze. Reading it slowly.)
(Biscuit gives a slow wag. Blue hour wag. Half speed.)
(The cat on the wall curls up. Biscuit curls up too. Solidarity.)
(Biscuit hears the clock's minute hand. Nobody else does.)
(Biscuit chases his own long shadow. It is winning.)
(Biscuit's shadow is the size of a horse tonight. He is delighted.)
(Biscuit inspects the fountain. Still wet. Good.)
(Biscuit stops at every shutter. Each one smells of a story.)
(Biscuit sits under the clock and waits for it to do something.)
(The clock chimes six. Biscuit chimes back. Woof.)
(Biscuit trots under the awning. Shade, then sun, then shade.)
(Biscuit counts the blue tiles by sniffing them. Twelve. Fourteen.)
(Biscuit lies on the warm tiles for exactly one second.)
(Biscuit tugs toward the café. Yusuf tugs toward the sea.)
(Biscuit waits for Henri and Odile to finish crossing. Gentleman.)
(Biscuit puts his chin on Odile's shoe. She allows it.)
(Biscuit hears Lucie's bell somewhere. Ears up. Tail up.)
(Biscuit's ears glow pink in the low sun. Very handsome.)
(Biscuit sneezes at a cypress. The cypress does not mind.)
(Biscuit finds a crumb of croissant. The day is complete.)
(Biscuit carries a pinecone like a trophy. Nobody asked.)
(Biscuit drops the pinecone at Yusuf's feet. A gift.)
(Biscuit tilts his head at the string lights. Not on yet.)
(The string lights blink on. Biscuit barks once, impressed.)
(Biscuit remembers being small enough to fit in the bread basket.)
(Biscuit passes the bench where he learned to sit. Sits. Proud.)
(Biscuit sits like Yusuf taught him. Then like Biscuit taught him.)
(Biscuit greets a palm tree. Old friend. Bit tall.)
(Biscuit says good evening to every lamppost. Thorough.)
(Biscuit wags in a circle. Then the other way, to be fair.)
(Biscuit watches the fountain like it might throw him a ball.)
(Biscuit drinks from the low edge of the fountain. Fancy water.)
(Biscuit pauses at the kiosk. The kiosk smells of mint and paper.)
(Biscuit lies down in the one stripe of sun left. Expert.)
(Biscuit follows the stripe of sun across the square.)
(Biscuit trots on the zebra stripes of an awning shadow.)
(Biscuit hears a shutter close. Turns. Says goodnight to it.)
(A green shutter opens above. Biscuit wags up at it.)
(Someone waves from a window box. Biscuit wags at the geraniums.)
(Biscuit sniffs a terracotta pot. Basil. Excellent choice.)
(Biscuit is a lot of dog for such short legs. He knows.)
(Biscuit makes the lead into a zigzag. Art.)
(Biscuit stops. Sniffs. Considers. Moves on. A critic.)
(Biscuit approves of the evening. Four paws up.)
(Biscuit trots past Marcel's. Marcel bows. Biscuit bows back.)
(Biscuit sits by Marcel's chalkboard. Reads it. Hungry now.)
(Biscuit pretends a sugar cube fell. It did not. Worth a try.)
(Biscuit rests his head on the cool zinc of a bench leg.)
(Biscuit looks up at the zinc roofs. Gold. Possibly edible.)
(Biscuit trots in Inès' slipstream for three steps. Fast dog.)
(Inès runs past. Biscuit counts her laps too. Badly.)
(Biscuit wants to run with the runners. Then remembers dinner.)
(Biscuit sniffs Léo's sandal. Fountain, sand, ice cream.)
(Léo throws a stick. Biscuit brings back a better stick.)
(Biscuit lets Léo pat him for nine whole pats.)
(Biscuit noses Théo's pocket. Bread crust. Called it.)
(Camille scratches behind Biscuit's ear. His leg kicks. Bliss.)
(Biscuit looks at the sea. Big water. Good water. Not today.)
(Biscuit sits on the warm promenade stones. Toasty bottom.)
(Biscuit shakes. Dust goes everywhere, golden. Fireworks.)
(Biscuit's whiskers catch the sunlight. Little gold antennas.)
(Biscuit snorts at a gull. The gull snorts back. Even.)
(Biscuit pretends the gull is not there. Very mature.)
(Biscuit yawns hugely. Not tired. Just showing his teeth to the sun.)
(Biscuit pauses on the bridge of shade under a palm.)
(Biscuit trots along the railing posts. One, sniff. Two, sniff.)
(Biscuit puts both front paws on the low wall. Lookout.)
(Biscuit finds the cobble with the little shell in it. His cobble.)
(Biscuit greets the shell cobble every evening. Tradition.)
(Biscuit rolls on his back by the cypresses. Pure joy.)
(Biscuit gets up from the roll. Dignified, mostly.)
(Biscuit hops the gutter. Lands it. Waits for applause.)
(Henri claps for the gutter hop. Biscuit was right to wait.)
(Biscuit inspects a dropped flower. Bougainvillea. Fancy.)
(Biscuit carries the bougainvillea for Yusuf. Very romantic.)
(Biscuit offers his paw to the neighbour. Business done.)
(Biscuit sniffs the evening air. Bread, salt, warm stone.)
(Biscuit tracks the smell of supper somewhere. Third window.)
(Biscuit's tail sweeps the tiles clean. Helpful dog.)
(Biscuit trots faster near home. Then remembers: the long one.)
(Biscuit takes the stairs two at a time. Small stairs.)
(Biscuit leans on Yusuf's leg. Both of them watch the light.)
(Biscuit sniffs a postcard someone dropped. Smells like holiday.)
(Biscuit trots in a figure eight round two bollards. Show-off.)
(Biscuit's collar tag jingles. The fountain jingles back.)
(Biscuit sits for a treat. Then lies down for a bonus.)
(Biscuit gets the bonus. Life is very fair.)
(Biscuit closes his eyes in the sun. One ear keeps working.)
(Biscuit noses open a gap in the hedge. Shortcut. Approved.)
(Biscuit's nose twitches at the café's onion soup. Noted.)
(Biscuit trots past the clock at six thirty. Right on time.)
(Biscuit gives the visitor's suitcase a full inspection. Cleared.)
(Biscuit tows Yusuf past the bench. Hello, Henri! Bye, Henri!)
(Biscuit sits and looks golden. Because he is, right now.)
(Biscuit spots the cat on the wall. They nod. Old colleagues.)
(Biscuit counts the gulls on the railing. Seven. Good number.)
(A gull lands. Biscuit sits politely and waits his turn.)
(The wall cat blinks slowly. Biscuit blinks back, slower.)
(Biscuit trots beside his own long shadow. Two dogs now.)
(Biscuit hears the accordion. One ear up. Then both.)
(Biscuit stops for the accordion. Tail keeps the beat.)
(Biscuit sniffs Odile's crossword. Seven letters. Biscuit.)
(Biscuit checks the bench legs one by one. All present.)
(Biscuit leads Yusuf the long way. As agreed. By Biscuit.)
(Biscuit sits under the café table. Ready for crumbs.)
(Biscuit inspects a cypress. Five stars. Would sniff again.)
(The cat yawns on the warm wall. Biscuit yawns too. Contagious.)
(Biscuit watches a gull eat a crust. Respect between equals.)
(Biscuit pauses at the fountain. Listens. Approves the splash.)
(Trot, trot, sniff. Trot, trot, sniff. Evening rhythm.)
(Biscuit hears a page turn. Looks up. Hoping it is a menu.)
(Biscuit found a pine cone. It is the best pine cone.)
(The wall cat flicks its tail. Biscuit wags in reply. Chat.)
(Biscuit leads past the roses. Slows down. Smells all of them.)
(A gull calls. Biscuit answers with one tiny woof. Agreed.)
(Biscuit walks on the warm side of the promenade. Obviously.)
(Biscuit sits and listens to Marcel humming. Good song.)
(Biscuit sniffs a dropped olive. Decides it is for gulls.)
(Biscuit trots up to Lucie. Waits. Ding. Bliss.)
(Biscuit wags at Inès as she runs past. Cheering, really.)
(Biscuit stops dead. Sniffs the air. Someone is baking.)
(Biscuit sits for the sunset. Front row. His usual seat.)
(Biscuit tugs gently towards the café. A suggestion.)
(Biscuit watches the waiter's tray go by. Tracks it closely.)
(Biscuit hops the low step. Lands it. Small bow.)
(The cat descends from the wall. Biscuit makes room. Gentleman.)
(Biscuit trots ahead, then waits. Yusuf is slow but loved.)
(Biscuit sniffs a library book left on the bench. Well read.)
(Biscuit chooses left. Then right. Then left. Thorough.)
(Biscuit sneezes at a lavender bush. Delighted about it.)
(Biscuit examines a palm trunk. Very scratchy. Good palm.)
(Biscuit hears a guitar from a window. Sits. Tilts head.)
(Biscuit greets Camille's shoes, then Camille. Order matters.)
(Biscuit sniffs a chalk drawing. A sun. He approves.)
(Biscuit watches gulls glide. Wonders about wings. Briefly.)
(Biscuit's tail wags faster as the lamps start to warm.)
(Biscuit sits beside Théo at the railing. Two connoisseurs.)
(Biscuit leads Yusuf past the fountain twice. Once is not enough.)
(The wall cat is in the same spot as yesterday. Reassuring.)
(Biscuit sniffs the promenade like it is a long letter.)
(Biscuit puts one paw up on the bench. Asks nicely.)
(Biscuit trots with his nose high. Smells the whole evening.)
(Biscuit hears Henri fold his newspaper. Means a walk soon.)
(Biscuit finds a feather. Gives it to Yusuf. A gift.)
(Biscuit listens to the sea. Nods along. Very wise.)
(Biscuit trots past the arcade. The bleeps make him wag.)
(Biscuit sits beside the busker's hat. Helping, he thinks.)
(Biscuit stretches. Front paws, back paws. Off again.)
(Biscuit sniffs a crust under a café chair. Today's special.)
(Biscuit wags at a stranger. Now they are friends.)
(Biscuit leads proudly. Yusuf follows. As is right.)
(Biscuit lies flat on the warm stones. Solar powered.)
(Biscuit watches Odile knit. The wool moves. Fascinating.)
(Biscuit hears the piano from the café. Slows to a stroll.)
(Biscuit's lead goes slack. He is waiting for Yusuf. Patient.)
(Biscuit greets the lamp post he greeted this morning.)
(Biscuit trots along the railing, nose to the sea breeze.)
(Biscuit hears the church bell up the hill. Counts with ears.)
(Biscuit leads Yusuf to the warm wall. The cat moves over.)
(Biscuit watches a crossword pencil wiggle. Wants it. Politely.)
(Biscuit's little trot goes extra springy near the café.)
(Biscuit and the gulls watch the sun together. No squabbling.)
(Biscuit stops to admire the orange sky. Then a smell.)
(Biscuit hums along with Yusuf. Very low. Mostly a sigh.)
(Biscuit tows Yusuf towards the roses. Gently. Firmly.)
(Biscuit circles once, then sits. Nothing to do but glow.)
(The cat jumps down and walks beside Biscuit. A short parade.)
(Biscuit gives the bench a slow, happy tail thump.)
(Biscuit sits on the warm doormat. Then on the warmer one.)
(Biscuit stops for a gull feather. Leaves it. Generous.)
(Biscuit closes his eyes in the last sun. A very good boy.)
(Biscuit sits under the bench. Prime sandwich territory.)
(Biscuit rests his chin on Yusuf's knee. A formal request.)
(Biscuit watches the sandwich travel. Up. Down. Up.)
(A crumb falls. Biscuit was born for this moment.)
(Biscuit counts the bench slats with his nose. Six. Correct.)
(Biscuit lies in the bench's shadow. Exactly in it.)
(Biscuit moves to the sunny half. Then back. Perfect.)
(Biscuit tilts his head at the word lunch.)
(Biscuit sits so nicely. Look. Look how nicely.)
(One ear up for the sandwich, one down for the nap.)
(Biscuit receives the crust with great ceremony.)
(The crust is gone. Biscuit checks under the bench anyway.)
(Biscuit hops up beside Yusuf. Shared bench. Shared lunch?)
(Biscuit sighs the sigh of a dog who has had half a crust.)
(Biscuit guards the bench while Yusuf unwraps the paper.)
(The paper rustles. Biscuit's whole body listens.)
(Biscuit tucks his paws neatly. A very proper terrier.)
(Biscuit offers a paw. Then the other paw. Just in case.)
(Biscuit naps with one eyebrow on duty.)
(Biscuit leans on Yusuf's ankle. Best seat on the bench.)
(Biscuit licks the last crumb off the bench. Tidy dog.)
(Biscuit stares at the cheese. The cheese stares back.)
(The clock chimes. Biscuit counts along. Lunch, lunch, lunch.)
(Biscuit thumps his tail on the bench leg. Tok. Tok. Tok.)
(Biscuit decides the bench is his. Yusuf may stay.)
(Biscuit yawns so wide his ears fold back.)
(The pigeon and Biscuit, both waiting for crumbs. Partners.)
(Biscuit drinks from the bowl Marcel left. Merci, Marcel.)
(Biscuit spots the waiter's tray. Ears to full height.)
(Biscuit sits on the end of the bench like a little statue.)
(Biscuit gives the apple core a polite sniff. No, thank you.)
(Biscuit's nose twitches. Somebody ordered the croque.)
(Biscuit wriggles closer. Then closer. Then on Yusuf.)
(Biscuit gets the last bite. He knew he would.)
(Biscuit watches the fountain splash. Water is very busy.)
(Biscuit stretches long under the bench. Front paws. Back paws.)
(A gull lands on the next bench. Biscuit notes it, officially.)
(Biscuit and the gull share a long, respectful look.)
(The gull leaves first. Biscuit counts it as a win.)
(Biscuit puts one paw on the bench. Asking. Politely.)
(Biscuit is lifted onto the bench. Now he is a person.)
(Biscuit sits on the bench like a small mayor.)
(Biscuit surveys the promenade from the bench. All in order.)
(Biscuit dreams for one minute. Tail thumps once.)
(Biscuit wakes up, checks the sandwich situation, sleeps again.)
(Yusuf scratches the right ear. Biscuit offers the left too.)
(Yusuf reads. Biscuit reads the air. Both very busy.)
(Biscuit snores, very softly, under the bench.)
(Biscuit watches the cat wash a paw. Learns a lot.)
(Biscuit tries washing a paw too. Gives up. Licks Yusuf.)
(Biscuit sniffs Henri's shoe. Lemon tree, again. Good man.)
(Biscuit says hello to Odile's handbag. It smells of mints.)
(Biscuit rolls over on the warm tiles. Belly to the sun.)
(Odile pats Biscuit and says something French. He agrees.)
(Henri tips his hat to Biscuit. Biscuit bows, sort of.)
(Henri says a word out loud. Biscuit's ears go up. Not it.)
(Biscuit trots past the café, tail like a little flag.)
(Biscuit sniffs the blue shutters. They smell of paint and sun.)
(Biscuit finds the coolest tile on the square. Settles.)
(Biscuit drinks from the fountain's low step. Very fresh.)
(Biscuit barks once at the fountain fish. A friendly hello.)
(Biscuit stands under the awning. The stripy shade is best.)
(Biscuit sniffs a cypress. Taller than him. Smells taller too.)
(Biscuit hears the noon bell and sits. Twelve is a sitting time.)
(Biscuit trots in a circle, then lies down in the same spot.)
(Biscuit sneezes at a geranium. The geranium is fine.)
(Biscuit greets a pigeon by walking past it very slowly.)
(Biscuit follows a crumb trail to the café. Good trail.)
(Biscuit sniffs the string lights' pole. Last night was fun.)
(Biscuit sits under the string lights, unlit. Waiting for later.)
(Biscuit wags at the kiosk. The kiosk wags back, sort of.)
(Biscuit sniffs the kiosk corner. Newspapers and peaches.)
(Biscuit naps in a stripe of sun between two shadows.)
(Biscuit sniffs a sandal. Then the other sandal. A matched pair.)
(Biscuit waits at the café door. Patience has a smell: ham.)
(Biscuit's tail goes faster when Léo runs by.)
(Biscuit chases his own shadow. It is very short at noon.)
(Biscuit sniffs the palm tree. It smells like holidays.)
(Biscuit pads across the hot tiles quickly. Hop, hop, shade.)
(Biscuit sits by the menu board. Reads the specials. Ham.)
(Biscuit gets a scratch from Lucie. Ears go soft.)
(Biscuit sees Lucie's bike. Ears up. Waiting for the ding.)
(Biscuit sniffs a lemon that fell. Too sour. Still a lemon.)
(Biscuit pushes a lemon along with his nose. A new game.)
(Biscuit and the lemon reach the fountain. Game complete.)
(Biscuit lies flat as a rug by the fountain. A happy rug.)
(Biscuit watches the café chairs. Someone will drop something.)
(A croissant flake drifts down. Biscuit catches it. Bravo.)
(Biscuit sniffs a postcard rack. Many places. All far. Here wins.)
(Biscuit sits in the exact middle of the square. Central dog.)
(Biscuit gets a crust of baguette from Théo. Best friend now.)
(Biscuit poses for Théo's pencil. Chin up. Profile side.)
(Biscuit lifts his nose at the bakery breeze. Bread o'clock.)
(Biscuit follows the smell of fresh bread three steps. Stops.)
(Biscuit sniffs a flower pot on a doorstep. Approves strongly.)
(Biscuit sits for the photo. Then moves. Then sits again.)
(Biscuit greets the camera with his whole back half.)
(Biscuit drinks, then shakes. The square gets a little rain.)
(Biscuit stands in the fountain spray. Instant rainbow dog.)
(Biscuit dries in the sun like a little towel.)
(Biscuit trots after Léo, then remembers he is on duty.)
